search_strategy: Wrote two helper scripts against the Mattermost API: /tmp/mms.py (search API, 'step ledger'/'reason' terms) to find an initial hit, then /tmp/mmc.py (full paginated channel pull) to dump every channel (code-review 3236 lines, cookbooks 773, engineering 2477, general 261, help 150, incidents 270, pipeline 2008, releases 701, viewer 338, etc.) to local /tmp/chat/*.txt files. From there it worked almost entirely by grep across the local dump ('reason', 'CHECKPOINT_REASONS', 'canonical_reasons', 'tinker', 'warmup', 'step ledger|dataset_signature|optimizer step|accumulation') followed by sed -n prints of the surrounding 20-80 lines whenever a hit landed, iterating channel-by-channel and date-window-by-date-window until each thread read as settled. It separately grepped /tmp/wiki for the same vocabulary (found nothing relevant) and never read mail. This is thorough and recovered 42 of 47 remarks, but it was grep-first: every remark whose distinctive words never appeared in a query the agent typed was invisible even though the full channel text sat locally on disk (e.g. the May-30 code-review PR-663 thread, never grepped for '663' or 'min_lr_ratio' against chat). It did not re-print code-review.txt, cookbooks.txt or general.txt past the ranges its first pass already found, so later-dated remarks in already-visited channels were the ones it lost.
